findings.evidence: The definition is at line 363 and the only characterization at lines 371–375 is an `EventuallyEq` of representatives; Mathlib provides `HilbertBasis.coe_mkOfOrthogonalEqBot` at `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/l2Space.lean:533`.
findings.fix: Add a `[simp]` `prodHilbertBasis_apply` equality using `HilbertBasis.coe_mkOfOrthogonalEqBot`, and derive `coeFn_prodHilbertBasis` from it plus `coeFn_L2prodMul`.
findings.issue: `prodHilbertBasis` only has the a.e. representative theorem `coeFn_prodHilbertBasis`; there is no `[simp]` theorem stating `prodHilbertBasis b₁ b₂ (i,j) = L2prodMul (b₁ i) (b₂ j)`, so inner-product and basis-expansion consumers cannot rewrite it through the tensor API.

summary: The product basis lacks a direct, simplifiable characterization as an `Lp` vector, forcing consumers to reason through representatives or unfold the opaque definition.
